title: A heat-stable COVID-19 vaccine from an IISc start-up
summary: Mynvax was founded in 2017 by IISc professor Raghavan Varadarajan and alumnus Gautham Nadig, and incubated at IISc. Its vaccine formulations stayed stable at 37 °C for up to a month and at 100 °C for up to 90 minutes, so they would not need a cold chain. In 2021 it signed agreements to raise a $4.2 million Series A round led by Accel.

title: Gallium-nitride chips made in India
summary: AGNIT Semiconductors was founded in 2019 and incubated at IISc, and licenses background IP from IISc. It makes gallium-nitride (GaN) wafers and RF transistors and amplifiers; its markets include defence, space and telecom.

title: Industry-funded research: the Robert Bosch Centre for Cyber-Physical Systems
summary: In 2011 Bosch made a ₹115 crore (€22 million) grant to IISc over ten years, which set up the Robert Bosch Centre for Cyber-Physical Systems.

title: Instruments for India's first astronomy satellite
summary: ISRO launched AstroSat on 28 September 2015. TIFR developed three of its five payloads: the Large Area X-ray Proportional Counter (LAXPC), the Cadmium Zinc Telluride Imager (CZTI) and the Soft X-ray Telescope (SXT). The papers here describe and calibrate those instruments and use their data.

title: Monsoon research used by India's forecasting agencies
summary: India's seasonal and extended-range monsoon forecasts come from models built under the Ministry of Earth Sciences' Monsoon Mission and run operationally by IMD. IISc's monsoon papers are cited by the agencies in that chain: IMD, IITM Pune, NCMRWF and INCOIS. This shows use of the research by forecasters, not a causal link to a specific forecast.
